title: Typed lower-shriek counits on polynomial-presentation sites
statement:
Let $A\to B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Choose a common infinite cardinal bound containing the three rings and all variable sets used below, and small skeletons in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C_{T/S}$ be the opposite category of polynomial $S$-algebras $P$ with an $S$-algebra map $P\to T$; a morphism in the non-opposite category is an $S$-algebra map commuting with these augmentations. Let $\mathcal E=\mathcal C_{C/B/A}$ be the opposite category of pairs $U=(P\to B,Q\to C)$, with $P$ polynomial over $A$, $Q$ polynomial over $P$, and $Q\to C$ compatible with $P\to B\to C$; morphisms before taking opposites are pairs of compatible $A$-algebra maps $P\to P'$, $Q\to Q'$ commuting with both augmentations and with $P\to Q$. Put $\mathcal C_1=\mathcal C_{B/A}$, $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal C_{C/A}$, $\mathcal C_3=\mathcal C_{C/B}$. Give all four categories the topology generated by singleton identity coverings (equivalently the pretopology of singleton isomorphisms), so sheaves are presheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Define
$$u_1(U)=(P\to B),\quad u_2(U)=(Q\to C),\quad u_3(U)=(Q\otimes_P B\to C).$$
Their action on morphisms is the induced algebra map, with arrows reversed; $Q$ is polynomial over $A$ and $Q\otimes_P B$ is polynomial over $B$. On $\mathcal C_i$ write $\mathcal O^{(i)}$ for the ring presheaf sending a presentation to its polynomial algebra, $R_1=B$, $R_2=R_3=C$, and $\mathcal O^{(i)}\to\underline{R_i}$ for its augmentation. The induced geometric morphism $g_i:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_i)$ has inverse image precomposition with $u_i$, direct image its right adjoint. Its inverse image is exact on module presheaves with pulled-back rings. Put $\mathcal O_i=g_i^{-1}\mathcal O^{(i)}$; explicitly their values at $U$ are $P,Q,Q\otimes_P B$. The variable-structural-ring morphism $g_i^{\mathrm{str}}:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),\mathcal O_i)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_i),\mathcal O^{(i)})$ has identity structural map $g_i^{-1}\mathcal O^{(i)}=\mathcal O_i$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. The augmentations $\mathcal O_i\to\underline{R_i}$ are the displayed maps to $B,C,C$; the additional coefficient map is $\underline B\to\underline C$.
For any commutative coefficient ring $R$, separately let $g_i^R:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),\underline R)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_i),\underline R)$ have identity structural map. Write $\pi^R,\pi_i^R$ for the constant-coefficient morphisms to $(*,R)$, with constant inverse images, so $\pi^R=\pi_i^R g_i^R$. All modules are sheaves of left modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The constant-coefficient $g_{i,!}^R$ is left Kan extension along $u_i^{op}$, i.e. the left adjoint to precomposition, and $Lg_{i,!}^R$ is its total left derived functor on $D(\underline R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; $L\pi_!^R$ is derived colimit as in [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. The adjunction counits
$$Lg_{i,!}^R g_i^{-1}K\longrightarrow K\quad(i=1,2,3)$$
are isomorphisms for every module presheaf $K$ on $\mathcal C_i$ in degree zero. Consequently the canonical maps
$$c_i(K):L\pi_!^R(g_i^{-1}K)\longrightarrow L\pi_{i,!}^R K$$
are isomorphisms in $D(R)$, natural in $K$. Their bar representatives are exactly $(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)\mapsto(u_iU_n\to\cdots\to u_iU_0,x)$ from [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. The same claims hold for abelian presheaves with $R=\mathbf Z$. These comparisons concern constant-coefficient module categories; the variable structural rings above specify the differential sheaves and their augmentation actions.

proof.text: The polynomial formulas define the three functors: writing $P=A[S]$ and $Q=P[T]$ gives $Q=A[S\amalg T]$ and $Q\otimes_P B=B[T]$. A functor between these presheaf sites is continuous and cocontinuous, since covers are generated by identities. Precomposition preserves kernels and cokernels objectwise; apply the cited derived-adjunction theorem with the constant ring $\underline R$. It supplies each $Lg_{i,!}^R\dashv g_i^{-1}$ with its canonical counit. For the variable rings, precomposition gives respectively $P,Q,Q\otimes_P B$ and the identity structural map; their augmentations and the coefficient map $B\to C$ are the specified algebra maps. Thus these structural rings are distinct from the constant coefficient ring used in the counit calculations.

source.place: Tags 07AC and 08PH; constant-ring case of the continuous/cocontinuous derived adjunction.

proof.text: Fix $V\in\mathcal C_i$. The comma formula computes $(Lg_{i,!}^Rg_i^{-1}K)(V)$ by the bar complex on $\mathcal I_V=(V\downarrow u_i)$, with coefficient $K(u_iU)$ at $(U,a)$. Its counit augmentation sends $((U,a),x)$ to $K(a)x$. We will prove this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism for every $V$. These are precisely the components of the counit, so their quasi-isomorphisms prove the presheaf counit is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08PK, specialized to the base site consisting of one point; the comma convention is V to u_i(U).

proof.text: For $i=1$, define $s_1(P\to B)=(P\to B,P\to C)$. The ring maps $P\xrightarrow{1}P$ and $P\to Q$ define a natural arrow $U\to s_1u_1U$ in the opposite category, whose image under $u_1$ is the identity. On $\mathcal I_V$ let $p(U,a)=(u_1U,a)$ in $\mathcal J_V=(V\downarrow\mathcal C_1)$ and $s(W,a)=(s_1W,a)$. Then $ps=1$ and these arrows give $1\Rightarrow sp$. The coefficient presheaf is pulled back from $\mathcal J_V$, and restriction along this transformation is the identity on $K(W)$. The cited prism-homotopy clause makes the bar maps of $p,s$ mutually inverse on homology and compatible with the counit augmentations. In $\mathcal J_V$ the object $(V,1)$ is initial. Prepending its unique arrow to the first vertex of a bar chain contracts the augmented complex to $K(V)$: the first face is the original chain and all other faces cancel the corresponding insertion after a face; in degree zero the remaining term is restriction $K(W)\to K(V)$. Hence the counit augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism for $i=1$.

source.place: Tag 08QW, case i=1; explicit section and bar contraction in place of the fibred-category computation.

proof.text: For $i=2$, put $s_2(Q\to C)=(A\to B,Q\to C)$, which is an object because $Q$ is polynomial over $A$. The compatible ring maps $A\to P$ and $1_Q$ define $U\to s_2u_2U$ and project to $1_Q$. On $\mathcal I_V$ the functor $p(U,a)=(u_2U,a)$ to $\mathcal J_V=(V\downarrow\mathcal C_2)$ has section $s(W,a)=(s_2W,a)$; $ps=1$ and the displayed arrows give $1\Rightarrow sp$ with identity coefficient restrictions. By the cited prism homotopy their bar maps are inverse on homology. The unique arrows from $(V,1)$ in $\mathcal J_V$ give the same insertion contraction: prepend $(V,1)$ to a chain; the first face recovers that chain, the other terms cancel against insertion after a face, and the augmented degree-zero term is $K(a)x$. Thus the counit at $V$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This avoids the proposed lift $(P,Q')$ in the source: a polynomial $A$-algebra $Q'$ with a map $Q\to Q'$ need not be polynomial over $P$, so that proposed lift need not be an object.

source.place: Tag 08QW, case i=2; corrected argument using the explicit section and the bar prism homotopy.

proof.text: For $i=3$, fix $V=(\overline Q\to C)$, where $\overline Q$ is polynomial over $B$. An object of $\mathcal I_V$ is a pair $(P,Q)$ and a compatible $B$-algebra map $Q\otimes_P B\to\overline Q$. Such a map is exactly a map $Q\to\overline Q$ agreeing on $P$ with $P\to B\to\overline Q$: the correspondence is $q\otimes b\mapsto\gamma(q)b$. This identifies $\mathcal I_V$ with the opposite category of polynomial presentation pairs for $A\to B\to\overline Q$, including morphisms, by the same tensor universal property. Define a presheaf $\overline K$ on polynomial $B$-algebras augmented to $\overline Q$ by $\overline K(T\to\overline Q)=K(T\to\overline Q\to C)$. Under this identification the comma coefficient is exactly $v^{-1}\overline K$, and the counit augmentation is induced by $Q\otimes_P B\to\overline Q$.

source.place: Tag 08QW, case i=3: comma category I_U and its coefficient presheaf; the base is B, not C.

proof.text: Apply the polynomial-target lemma to $A\to B$ with polynomial target $\overline Q$ and coefficient presheaf $\overline K$. Its augmentation identifies the comma derived colimit with $\overline K(\overline Q\xrightarrow{1}\overline Q)[0]=K(V)[0]$. By its explicit augmentation clause, the map is exactly $((U,a),x)\mapsto K(a)x$, so it is the counit from Step 2, not just an unspecified isomorphism of its source and target. The comma formula now proves the third counit isomorphism. All comma categories are small under the fixed size convention, and the polynomial-target lemma applies because the target in this calculation is the polynomial algebra $\overline Q$, regardless of whether the original $C$ is polynomial over $B$.

source.place: Tags 08QV and 08QW, case i=3; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08PK.

proof.text: The composite $L\pi_{i,!}^R Lg_{i,!}^R$ is left adjoint to the composite of the exact right adjoints, namely the constant-presheaf functor on $\mathcal E$. The bar theorem gives $L\pi_!^R$ as another left adjoint to that same functor. The adjunction bijections therefore identify them uniquely, with the identity on the common right adjoint. Applying $L\pi_{i,!}^R$ to the counit isomorphism of Steps 3,4,6 gives $L\pi_!^R g_i^{-1}K\to L\pi_{i,!}^RK$ as an isomorphism. Its adjoint, using the composite adjunction, is the pullback of the unit $K\to\operatorname{const}(L\pi_{i,!}^RK)$: the intermediate unit followed by the pulled-back counit cancels by the triangle identity. This is the canonical reindexing map of the bar theorem, which for $t=1_{g_i^{-1}K}$ sends $(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$ to $(u_iU_n\to\cdots\to u_iU_0,x)$. Thus both the canonical map and its representative agree with the statement. Adjunction units, counits and these bar maps are natural in $K$.

source.place: Tags 08PF, 08PG and 08PH; uniqueness of left adjoints and the triangle identities identify the canonical map.

proof.text: With $R=\mathbf Z$, a module presheaf is an abelian presheaf, and every functor, augmentation, bar differential and inserted-chain homotopy above is a homomorphism of abelian groups. Thus the same assertions hold for abelian presheaves. The variable-ring structural maps and their augmentations were already computed objectwise in Step 1; no extension-of-scalars assertion for them is being substituted for a constant-coefficient comparison.

source.place: Tag 08PH, agreement of constant-coefficient module and abelian constructions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q54-f17c119c1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, the cited statements (lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar, lem-trf-continuous-cocontinuous-derived-shriek) and Stacks cotangent.tex 08QR, 08QV and 08QW and sites-cohomology.tex 08PG, 08PH, 08PJ, 08PK, 08Q9 and lemma-initial-final, in full. The live item is still unsplit and the cited statements are unchanged live. The item statement only clarifies the topology wording; it matches the bar node and is not weakened. The coefficient categories (constant R vs. the variable structural rings) are kept apart, and the 12-node via chain is kept. Steps 3 and 4: s_1=(P->B,P->C) and s_2=(A->B,Q->C) are valid objects, u_i maps the arrows U->s_iu_iU to identities, and ps=1. The bar node's eta-homotopy clause gives homotopy inverses, and the initial (V,1) in (V|C_i) contracts the augmented bar complex. I checked the degree-0 boundary (W,x)-(V,K(a)x). The E7 source error is confirmed on A=k, P=Q=k[x], B=C=k, Q'=k: the 08QW lift (P,Q') is not an object because Q' is not polynomial over P. The repair does not need fibredness. Step 5: I_V is identified with C_{Qbar/B/A} by the tensor universal property, the augmentation to C is forced, morphisms agree, and the coefficient is v^{-1}Kbar with base B. Step 6: (id_Qbar) is initial in D, so the 08QV node's augmentation is exactly ((U,a),x)->K(a)x, the counit itself (E5). There is no cycle. Step 7 identifies Lpi_! with Lpi_{i,!}Lg_{i,!} by uniqueness of adjoints, and the triangle identity gives the 08PH bar map, which repairs the E5 fault of Q29 and Q69. New nodes: the comma node (08PK over a point) has the correct direction (V->uU), contravariant restriction and a typed counit. I tested it on u=id and on an empty source, and it makes no general claim that the counit is an isomorphism. The polynomial-top node is 08QV with an explicit augmentation; I tested it on E empty or infinite, A=B, the zero ring and the zero coefficient. Neither node restates the item, and neither duplicates bar, change-rings, simplicial-derived-colimit (08Q9) or the derived-shriek existence node; rg over the DAG found no 08PK or 08QV node. Both have three search kinds, created.item set to this item, and blueprint.from/via set to the ancestor with the item prepended. All citations are in unit sk-i-curve-zero, there are no tool_uses and no SGA. Advisory: the new nodes lack lean_audit, which is common on landed Q nodes, so I did not repair it.
